title: Sharing a place
hook: Animals can use the same place at different times.

knows: Animals interact with other organisms and their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: In a toy habitat, species A feeds from 6–8 and species B feeds from 18–20. Do the stated feeding intervals overlap?

misconception: One observation or model rule gives a complete answer about nature.
objective: In a toy habitat, species A feeds from 6–8 and species B feeds from 18–20. Do the stated feeding intervals overlap?

claims.text: In a toy habitat, species A feeds from 6–8 and species B feeds from 18–20. Do the stated feeding intervals overlap? The marked intervals 6–8 and 18–20 are separate on the same 24-hour clock. This stated timing alone does not prove whether the species compete in other ways.
claims.source: Unverified reference lead for independent check: OpenStax Biology 2e, ecology and populations, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e . Exact claim-specific sources have not been verified.

claims.text: The panels depict a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
In a toy habitat, one animal feeds 8–10 and another 14–16. Do those stated intervals overlap? The two stipulated time intervals do not overlap.
